v.s: [The time of] their account has approached for the people, while they are in heedlessness turning away.
v.c: ˹The time of˺ people’s judgment has drawn near, yet they are heedlessly turning away.

q: to any new advice that comes to them from their Rabb
(they mockingly pretend to be listening intently)...
v.s: No mention [i.e., revelation] comes to them anew from their Lord except that they listen to it while they are at play
v.c: Whatever new reminder comes to them from their Lord, they only listen to it jokingly,

q: (they have no intention of heeding the advice).
(He is not a Prophet but a man who has learnt magic. Therefore, the effect that the Qur'aan has on people is not because it is from Allaah but because of the magic that he practises)
(with your own eyes? Will you believe in it knowing that it is magic)?”
v.s: With their hearts distracted. And those who do wrong conceal their private conversation, [saying], "Is this [Prophet] except a human being like you? So would you approach magic while you are aware [of it]?"
v.c: with their hearts ˹totally˺ distracted. The evildoers would converse secretly, ˹saying,˺ “Is this ˹one˺ not human like yourselves? Would you fall for ˹this˺ witchcraft, even though you can ˹clearly˺ see?”

q: “My Rabb knows the speech in the heavens and the earth, and He is All Hearing, All Knowing”.
(He therefore knows what you discuss in secret and will punish you for it.)
v.s: He [the Prophet (ﷺ)] said, "My Lord knows whatever is said throughout the heaven and earth, and He is the Hearing, the Knowing."
v.c: The Prophet responded, “My Lord ˹fully˺ knows every word spoken in the heavens and the earth. For He is the All-Hearing, All-Knowing.”

q: (whose words have appeal but lack truth)! (If he wishes to prove to us that he is a Rasool,)
He should bring us an Aayah
like the ones sent with the
v.s: But they say, "[The revelation is but] a mixture of false dreams; rather, he has invented it; rather, he is a poet. So let him bring us a sign just as the previous [messengers] were sent [with miracles]."
v.c: Yet they say, “This ˹Quran˺ is a set of confused dreams! No, he has fabricated it! No, he must be a poet! So let him bring us a ˹tangible˺ sign like those ˹prophets˺ sent before.”

q: None of the towns that We destroyed before them had Imaan
Will these people now have Imaan
(when they see the same miracles)? (Just as previous nations were destroyed when they refused to believe in the miracles they requested, all Mushrikeen also stand to suffer the same fate).
v.s: Not a [single] city which We destroyed believed before them, so will they believe?
v.c: Not a ˹single˺ society We destroyed before them ever believed ˹after receiving the signs˺. Will these ˹pagans˺ then believe?

q: to whom We have sent revelation, so ask those who have knowledge
if you do not possess any knowledge
v.s: And We sent not before you, [O Muhammad], except men to whom We revealed [the message], so ask the people of the message [i.e., former scriptures] if you do not know.
v.c: We did not send ˹messengers˺ before you ˹O Prophet˺ except mere men inspired by Us. If you ˹polytheists˺ do not know ˹this already˺, then ask those who have knowledge ˹of the Scriptures˺.

q: mere bodies who do not eat food and they did not live forever.
(Like all human beings, the Ambiyaa ﵊ also needed to eat and drink and they also had to die)
v.s: And We did not make them [i.e., the prophets] forms not eating food, nor were they immortal [on earth].
v.c: We did not give those messengers ˹supernatural˺ bodies that did not need food, nor were they immortal.

q: Then We made true the promise to them
(that they will be rescued from the Kuffaar and saved from the punishment that will destroy the Kuffaar),
and destroyed those who transgressed the limits
v.s: Then We fulfilled for them the promise, and We saved them and whom We willed and destroyed the transgressors.
v.c: Then We fulfilled Our promise to them, saving them along with whoever We willed and destroying the transgressors.

q: We have certainly revealed to you people a Book
for you. Will you still not understand?
v.s: We have certainly sent down to you a Book [i.e., the Qur’ān] in which is your mention. Then will you not reason?
v.c: We have surely revealed to you a Book, in which there is glory for you. Will you not then understand?

q: How many were the oppressive towns
and We then created another nation after them.
(Therefore, no nation should think that they are indispensable because We can destroy them in the same manner and create others to replace them.)
v.s: And how many a city which was unjust have We shattered and produced after it another people.
v.c: ˹Imagine˺ how many societies of wrongdoers We have destroyed, raising up other people after them!

q: (in an effort to escape the punishment).
v.s: And when they [i.e., its inhabitants] perceived Our punishment, at once they fled from it.
v.c: When the wrongdoers sensed ˹the arrival of˺ Our torment, they started to run away from their cities.

q: (The angels bringing the punishment then told them,)
“Do not flee, but return to the things that gave you pleasure
(the luxuries that kept you from accepting Imaan)
and to your homes. Perhaps you may be asked
(by later generations about what happened to you. Of course, you and whatever you treasured will not be there to answer their questions).”
v.s: [Some angels said], "Do not flee but return to where you were given luxury and to your homes - perhaps you will be questioned."
v.c: ˹They were told,˺ “Do not run away! Return to your luxuries and your homes, so you may be questioned ˹about your fate˺.”

q: They said, “Woe be to us! We were oppressors
(we oppressed ourselves by inviting this punishment)!”
v.s: They said, "O woe to us! Indeed, we were wrongdoers."
v.c: They cried, “Woe to us! We have surely been wrongdoers.”

q: (like a doused fire without the pride they once possessed).
v.s: And that declaration of theirs did not cease until We made them [as] a harvest [mowed down], extinguished [like a fire].
v.c: They kept repeating their cry until We mowed them down, ˹leaving them˺ lifeless.

q: We have not created the heavens and the earth for idle amusement
(without apurpose). (Every creation of Allaah has a purpose, one of these purposes being that each creation is an example of Allaah's might and great power.)
v.s: And We did not create the heaven and earth and that between them in play.
v.c: We did not create the heavens and the earth and everything in between for sport.

q: If We intended to create a toy
We would have done so from Our side
(We would have created something simple instead of the magnificent heavens and earth)
if We were to really do so
(it would have been unnecessary to create anything so elaborate. It therefore follows that the heavens and earth are not mere toys and that there are great lessons to be learnt from them).
v.s: Had We intended to take a diversion, We could have taken it from [what is] with Us - if [indeed] We were to do so.
v.c: Had We intended to take ˹some˺ amusement, We could have found it in Our presence, if that had been Our Will.

q: (By pondering about the marvellous creation of Allaah, people are able to realise the truth of Towheed, which leads them to accept Imaan. By doing this, they are able to stay away from all types of falsehood. Referring to this, Allaah says,)
(than creating the whole of creation in vain, it is by means of the creation that)
shattering its head, after which it
(from a person's life because as a Mu'min, he shuns falsehood).
be destroyed because of what you concoct
v.s: Rather, We dash the truth upon falsehood, and it destroys it, and thereupon it departs. And for you is destruction from that which you describe.
v.c: In fact, We hurl the truth against falsehood, leaving it crushed, and it quickly vanishes. And woe be to you for what you claim!

q: belongs whoever is in the heavens and
who are with Him are not ashamed
to worship Him, nor do they tire
v.s: To Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth. And those near Him [i.e., the angels] are not prevented by arrogance from His worship, nor do they tire.
v.c: To Him belong all those in the heavens and the earth. And those nearest to Him are not too proud to worship Him, nor do they tire.

q: They glorify Him night and day without being lax
v.s: They exalt [Him] night and day [and] do not slacken.
v.c: They glorify ˹Him˺ day and night, never wavering.

q: Aaliha from the earth who can resurrect
(who can give life to the dead)? (It is obvious that their gods cannot do this. They are therefore not fit to be worshipped.)
v.s: Or have they [i.e., men] taken for themselves gods from the earth who resurrect [the dead]?
v.c: Or have they taken gods from the earth, who can raise the dead?

q: If there were other Aaliha but Allaah in the heavens and the earth, the

(because no two or more persons can think in the same way. Had there been many gods, each would have different opinions about running the system of the universe. It would therefore be impossible to see the system of the universe functioning as perfectly and flawlessly as it does. The finely tuned manner in which everything occurs makes it apparent that there is only One Allaah in control of everything).
Allaah, the Rabb of the Arsh, is Pure from
v.s: Had there been within them [i.e., the heavens and earth] gods besides God, they both would have been ruined. So exalted is God, Lord of the Throne, above what they describe.
v.c: Had there been other gods besides Allah in the heavens or the earth, both ˹realms˺ would have surely been corrupted. So Glorified is Allah, Lord of the Throne, far above what they claim.

q: will not be questioned about what He does
(because He is above all and everything He does is perfect, most appropriate and above questioning),
(about the actions they carry out in this world).
v.s: He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned.
v.c: He cannot be questioned about what He does, but they will ˹all˺ be questioned.

q: (to prove that these gods deserve to be worshipped)!”
is a reminder to those with me
(reminding them that none but Allaah deserves to be worshipped),
and a reminder to those before me
(reminding them that the same reminder was given to them in the previous scriptures).
But most of them do not know the truth
because of which they turn away
v.s: Or have they taken gods besides Him? Say, [O Muhammad], “Produce your proof. This [Qur’ān] is the message for those with me and the message of those before me.” But most of them do not know the truth, so they are turning away.
v.c: Or have they taken other gods besides Him? Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Show ˹me˺ your proof. Here is ˹the Quran,˺ the Reminder for those with me; along with ˹earlier Scriptures,˺ the Reminder for those before me.” But most of them do not know the truth, so they turn away.

q: We sent revelation to every Rasool before you
that, “Without doubt there is no Ilaah but Me, so worship Me only.”
v.s: And We sent not before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that, “There is no deity except Me, so worship Me.”
v.c: We never sent a messenger before you ˹O Prophet˺ without revealing to him: “There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Me, so worship Me ˹alone˺.”

q: (the angels whom they say are Allaah's children)
(of Allaah and one's children can obviously not be one's slaves).
v.s: And they say, “The Most Merciful has taken a son.” Exalted is He! Rather, they are [but] honoured servants.
v.c: And they say, “The Most Compassionate has offspring!” Glory be to Him! In fact, those ˹angels˺ are only ˹His˺ honoured servants,

q: do not speak before Him and duly carry out His orders
v.s: They cannot precede Him in word, and they act by His command.
v.c: who do not speak until He has spoken, ˹only˺ acting at His command.

q: He knows what is before them and what is behind them
and only the one with whom He is pleased will be able to intercede
(on behalf of anyone on the Day of Qiyaamah). (In fact)
They tremble with fear for Him.
v.s: He knows what is [presently] before them and what will be after them, and they cannot intercede except on behalf of one whom He approves. And they, from fear of Him, are apprehensive.
v.c: He ˹fully˺ knows what is ahead of them and what is behind them. They do not intercede except for whom He approves, and they tremble in awe of Him.

q: Whoever of them has to say, “I am an Ilaah besides Him
then We shall punish him in Jahannam. Thus do We punish the wrongdoers
v.s: And whoever of them should say, "Indeed, I am a god besides Him" - that one We would recompense with Hell. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers.
v.c: Whoever of them were to say, “I am a god besides Him,” they would be rewarded with Hell by Us. This is how We reward the wrongdoers.

q: Do the Kuffaar not see that the skies and the earth were once closed
(no rain fell from the sky and no plants grew on earth),
And We created every living thing from water. Will they still not accept Imaan?
v.s: Have those who disbelieved not considered that the heavens and the earth were a joined entity, and We separated them and made from water every living thing? Then will they not believe?
v.c: Do the disbelievers not realize that the heavens and earth were ˹once˺ one mass then We split them apart? And We created from water every living thing. Will they not then believe?

q: on the earth so that it does not shake with them
and We have made wide roads on earth so that they be guided
(in their travels from place to place).
v.s: And We placed within the earth firmly set mountains, lest it should shift with them, and We made therein [mountain] passes [as] roads that they might be guided.
v.c: And We have placed firm mountains upon the earth so it does not shake with them, and made in it broad pathways so they may find their way.

q: And We have made the sky a protected roof
(which Allaah safeguards to protect man from deadly rays and meteors),
v.s: And We made the sky a protected ceiling, but they, from its signs, are turning away.
v.c: And We have made the sky a well-protected canopy, still they turn away from its signs.

q: It is Allaah Who created the night, the day, the sun and the moon, each swimming in its own orbit
(never straying from its orbit and never crossing the orbit of the other).
v.s: And it is He who created the night and the day and the sun and the moon; all [heavenly bodies] in an orbit are swimming.
v.c: And He is the One Who created the day and the night, the sun and the moon—each travelling in an orbit.

q: We have not prescribed eternal life for any human before you
(regardless of whether the others were Ambiyaa ﵊ or not. You will therefore pass away like all others).
(They will have to die as well. They therefore have nothing to be happy about when you pass away because whereas you will enjoy happiness in the next life, they will suffer only misery.)
v.s: And We did not grant to any man before you eternity [on earth]; so if you die - would they be eternal?
v.c: We have not granted immortality to any human before you ˹O Prophet˺: so if you die, will they live forever?

q: (to see whether you continue obeying Allaah in all conditions)
and you will return to Us
(after death when We shall evaluate how you performed in your tests).
v.s: Every soul will taste death. And We test you with evil and with good as trial; and to Us you will be returned.
v.c: Every soul will taste death. And We test you ˹O humanity˺ with good and evil as a trial, then to Us you will ˹all˺ be returned.

q: they merely wish to ridicule you.
“Is this the person who makes mention of who criticises your gods?”
They totally reject the mention of Ar Rahmaan.
v.s: And when those who disbelieve see you, [O Muhammad], they take you not except in ridicule, [saying], “Is this the one who mentions [i.e., insults] your gods?” And they are, at the mention of the Most Merciful, disbelievers.
v.c: When the disbelievers see you ˹O Prophet˺, they only make fun of you, ˹saying,˺ “Is this the one who speaks ˹ill˺ of your gods?” while they disbelieve at the mention of the Most Compassionate.

q: Man has been created from haste
(with a hasty nature, because of which he is always in a hurry to do things and expect to see quick results).
I shall shortly show you My Aayaat
(the punishment I have promised you for committing kufr),
v.s: Man was created of haste [i.e., impatience]. I will show you My signs [i.e., vengeance], so do not impatiently urge Me.
v.c: Humankind is made of haste. I will soon show you My signs, so do not ask Me to hasten them.

q: (in your claim that we will be punished for committing kufr)?”
v.s: And they say, "When is this promise, if you should be truthful?"
v.c: They ask ˹the believers˺, “When will this threat come to pass if what you say is true?”

q: If only the Kuffaar knew the time
they will neither be able to ward off the Fire from their faces, nor from their backs
They will also not be helped
(there). (If they had knowledge of this, they would not behave as they do.)
v.s: If those who disbelieved but knew the time when they will not avert the Fire from their faces or from their backs and they will not be aided...
v.c: If only the disbelievers knew that a time will come when they will not be able to keep the Fire off their faces or backs, nor will they be helped.

q: will come to them suddenly, totally dumbfounding them. Then they will neither be able to repel it, nor will they be granted any respite
v.s: Rather, it will come to them unexpectedly and bewilder them, and they will not be able to repel it, nor will they be reprieved.
v.c: In fact, the Hour will take them by surprise, leaving them stunned. So they will not be able to avert it, nor will it be delayed from them.

q: Undoubtedly, the Rusul before you were also ridiculed
(they were destroyed by Allaah's punishment). (The same will be the plight of those who ridicule you).
v.s: And already were messengers ridiculed before you, but those who mocked them were enveloped by what they used to ridicule.
v.c: ˹Other˺ messengers had already been ridiculed before you ˹O Prophet˺, but those who mocked them were overtaken by what they used to ridicule.

q: Ar Rahmaan each day and night?” However,
(despite knowing that none can protect them from Allaah's punishment)
they turn away from the Reminder of their Rabb
v.s: Say, "Who can protect you at night or by day from the Most Merciful?" But they are, from the remembrance of their Lord, turning away.
v.c: Ask ˹them, O Prophet,˺ “Who can defend you by day or by night against the Most Compassionate?” Still they turn away from the remembrance of their Lord.

q: Or do they have Aaliha that will protect
(their Aaliha are so helpless that they)
cannot even help themselves, nor will anyone align with them
v.s: Or do they have gods to defend them other than Us? They are unable [even] to help themselves, nor can they be protected from Us.
v.c: Or do they have gods—other than Us—that can protect them? They cannot ˹even˺ protect themselves, nor will they be aided against Us.

q: until a long period passed by them
(in which they revelled in their prosperity and failed to accept Imaan).
Do they not see that We gradually diminish the lands
(by giving more and more land to the Muslims through successive victories)?
(No, because the Muslims will have ultimate victory.)
v.s: But, [on the contrary], We have provided good things for these [disbelievers] and their fathers until life was prolonged for them. Then do they not see that We set upon the land, reducing it from its borders? So it is they who will overcome?
v.c: In fact, We have allowed enjoyment for these ˹Meccans˺ and their forefathers for such a long time ˹that they took it for granted˺. Do they not see that We gradually reduce ˹their˺ land from its borders? Is it they who will then prevail?

q: Say, “I warn you only with revelation
(from Allaah and not with my own words). (However, although the warnings are from Allaah)
(those who do not want to accept what they hear)
cannot hear the call when they are warned.”
v.s: Say, "I only warn you by revelation." But the deaf do not hear the call when they are warned.
v.c: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “I warn you only by revelation.” But the deaf cannot hear the call when they are warned!

q: of your Rabb's punishment has to afflict them, they will
certainly say, “May destruction overtake us! We were oppressors
v.s: And if [as much as] a whiff of the punishment of your Lord should touch them, they would surely say, "O woe to us! Indeed, we have been wrongdoers."
v.c: If they were touched by even a breath of your Lord’s torment, they would certainly cry, “Woe to us! We have really been wrongdoers.”

q: On the Day of Qiyaamah, We will erect the scales of justice
(to weigh the good and bad actions of people)
and no soul will be oppressed
in the least. Even if a deed
is equal to the weight of a mustard seed, We shall bring it
(and need no one else for the task).
v.s: And We place the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be treated unjustly at all. And if there is [even] the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it forth. And sufficient are We as accountant.
v.c: We will set up the scales of justice on the Day of Judgment, so no soul will be wronged in the least. And ˹even˺ if a deed is the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it forth. And sufficient are We as a ˹vigilant˺ Reckoner.

q: Without doubt, We had granted Moosa ﵊ and Haaroon ﵊ the Decider
(between right and wrong, namely the Torah, which was also),
v.s: And We had already given Moses and Aaron the criterion and a light and a reminder for the righteous
v.c: Indeed, We granted Moses and Aaron the standard ˹to distinguish between right and wrong˺—a light and a reminder for the righteous,

q: who fear their Rabb without seeing Him, and are fearful of Qiyaamah
v.s: Who fear their Lord unseen, while they are of the Hour apprehensive.
v.c: who are in awe of their Lord without seeing Him, and are fearful of the Hour.

q: is a blessed advice that We have revealed. Will you then reject it
v.s: And this [Qur’ān] is a blessed message which We have sent down. Then are you with it unacquainted?
v.c: And this ˹Quran˺ is a blessed reminder which We have revealed. Will you ˹pagans˺ then deny it?

q: We had granted Ibraheem ﵊ his correct course
and We were always aware of him
(We knew that he was worthy of being Our Rasool).
v.s: And We had certainly given Abraham his sound judgement before, and We were of him well-Knowing
v.c: And indeed, We had granted Abraham sound judgment early on, for We knew him well ˹to be worthy of it˺.

q: When he told his father and his people, “What are these statues
v.s: When he said to his father and his people, "What are these statues to which you are devoted?"
v.c: ˹Remember˺ when he questioned his father and his people, “What are these statues to which you are so devoted?”

v.s: They said, "We found our fathers worshippers of them."
v.c: They replied, “We found our forefathers worshipping them.”

q: said, “Verily you people and your forefathers are certainly in manifest error
v.s: He said, "You were certainly, you and your fathers, in manifest error."
v.c: He responded, “Indeed, you and your forefathers have been clearly astray.”

q: They said, “Do you bring us the truth or are you from the jesters
(are you serious about what you are saying or are you merely amusing us)?”
v.s: They said, "Have you come to us with truth, or are you of those who jest?"
v.c: They asked, “Have you come to us with the truth, or is this a joke?”

q: (than worshipping these idols, you should understand that)
your Rabb is the Rabb of the heavens and the earth, Who has created
(It is He Whom you should worship.)
I am of those who bear
v.s: He said, "[No], rather, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth who created them, and I, to that, am of those who testify.
v.c: He replied, “In fact, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, Who created them ˹both˺. And to that I bear witness.”

q: “By Allaah! I shall certainly devise a scheme against your idols
after you have turned your backs
v.s: And [I swear] by God, I will surely plan against your idols after you have turned and gone away."
v.c: ˹Then he said to himself,˺ “By Allah! I will surely plot against your idols after you have turned your backs and gone away.”

q: (when the people one day left town to celebrate a festival,)
(used an axe to break all the idols and)
but for the largest of them
(which he left intact with the axe hung around its neck)
so that they may turn towards him.

(Seeing it intact with the axe, they may think that it could be responsible for the damage. However, they would then immediately dispel this thought because they knew that the idols could do nothing. In this manner, Ibraheem ﵊ wished to bring to their attention that they are wrong to worship such useless things.)
v.s: So he made them into fragments, except a large one among them, that they might return to it [and question].
v.c: So he smashed them into pieces, except the biggest of them, so they might turn to it ˹for answers˺.

q: (After returning to the town and seeing their idols destroyed,)
exclaimed, “Who has done this to our gods? He is certainly from the wrong-doers!”
v.s: They said, "Who has done this to our gods? Indeed, he is of the wrongdoers."
v.c: They protested, “Who dared do this to our gods? It must be an evildoer!”

q: said, “We have heard a youth speak of
(saying that he intends to devise a scheme against them).
v.s: They said, "We heard a young man mention them who is called Abraham."
v.c: Some said, “We heard a young man, called Abraham, speaking ˹ill˺ of them.”

q: They said, “Bring him before the people so that
v.s: They said, "Then bring him before the eyes of the people that they may testify."
v.c: They demanded, “Bring him before the eyes of the people, so that they may witness ˹his trial˺.”

q: They asked, “Is it you who did this to our gods, O Ibraheem?”
v.s: They said, "Have you done this to our gods, O Abraham?"
v.c: They asked, “Was it you who did this to our gods, O Abraham?”

q: this large one has done it. Ask them
v.s: He said, "Rather, this - the largest of them - did it, so ask them, if they should [be able to] speak."
v.c: He replied ˹sarcastically˺, “No, this one—the biggest of them—did it! So ask them, if they can talk!”

q: (when they realised their foolishness in worshipping idols who cannot even talk)
v.s: So they returned to [blaming] themselves and said [to each other], "Indeed, you are the wrongdoers."
v.c: So they came back to their senses, saying ˹to one another˺, “You yourselves are truly the wrongdoers!”

q: saying, “You know very well that these
v.s: Then they reversed themselves, [saying], "You have already known that these do not speak!"
v.c: Then they ˹quickly˺ regressed to their ˹original˺ mind-set, ˹arguing,˺ “You already know that those ˹idols˺ cannot talk.”

q: worship besides Allaah such things that can neither profit you nor harm you?”
v.s: He said, "Then do you worship instead of God that which does not benefit you at all or harm you?
v.c: He rebuked ˹them˺, “Do you then worship—instead of Allah—what can neither benefit nor harm you in any way?

q: on you and those that you worship besides Allaah! Do you not understand
v.s: Uff to you and to what you worship instead of God. Then will you not use reason?"
v.c: Shame on you and whatever you worship instead of Allah! Do you not have any sense?”

q: (Embarrassed and not knowing what to do,)
your gods if you will do so
(if you want to do something).” (So they made a large fire which was so hot that none could approach it. They were then forced to catapult Ibraheem ﵊ into it.)
v.s: They said, "Burn him and support your gods - if you are to act."
v.c: They concluded, “Burn him up to avenge your gods, if you must act.”

q: We said, “O fire! Be cool and peaceful for Ibraheem.”
(As a result of this command, not even a hair of Ibraheem was burnt and he lived peacefully in the fire for some time.)
v.s: We [i.e., God] said, "O fire, be coolness and safety upon Abraham."
v.c: We ordered, “O fire! Be cool and safe for Abraham!”

q: Ibraheem ﵊, We made them the worst losers
(because he remained unharmed, while they did not achieve their objective and will suffer the consequences in the Aakhirah).
v.s: And they intended for him a plan [i.e., harm], but We made them the greatest losers.
v.c: They had sought to harm him, but We made them the worst losers.

q: to a land that We had blessed for all
v.s: And We delivered him and Lot to the land which We had blessed for the worlds [i.e., peoples].
v.c: Then We delivered him, along with Lot, to the land We had showered with blessings for all people.

q: Is'haaq ﵊ and a grandson, Ya'qoob ﵊. We made all of them righteous
v.s: And We gave him Isaac and Jacob in addition, and all [of them] We made righteous.
v.c: And We blessed him with Isaac ˹as a son˺ and Jacob ˹as a grandson˺, as an additional favour—making all of them righteous.

q: by Our orders, and We commanded them to perform good deeds, to establish salaah, and to pay zakaah. They were all Our
v.s: And We made them leaders guiding by Our command. And We inspired to them the doing of good deeds, establishment of prayer, and giving of zakāh; and they were worshippers of Us.
v.c: We ˹also˺ made them leaders, guiding by Our command, and inspired them to do good deeds, establish prayer, and pay alms-tax. And they were devoted to Our worship.

q: They were certainly evil and sinful
v.s: And to Lot We gave judgement and knowledge, and We saved him from the city that was committing wicked deeds. Indeed, they were a people of evil, defiantly disobedient.
v.c: And to Lot We gave wisdom and knowledge, and delivered him from the society engrossed in shameful practices. They were certainly an evil, rebellious people.

q: And We admitted him into Our mercy
He was indeed from among the righteous
v.s: And We admitted him into Our mercy. Indeed, he was of the righteous.
v.c: And We admitted him into Our mercy, ˹for˺ he was truly one of the righteous.

q: (accepted his du'aa by sending the flood to them).
So We rescued him and his family from tremendous distress
v.s: And [mention] Noah, when he called [to God] before [that time], so We responded to him and saved him and his family from the great affliction [i.e., the flood].
v.c: And ˹remember˺ when Noah had cried out to Us earlier, so We responded to him and delivered him and his family from the great distress.

q: And We granted him salvation from a nation who rejected Our Aayaat. They were indeed an evil nation, so We drowned all of them.
v.s: And We aided [i.e., saved] him from the people who denied Our signs. Indeed, they were a people of evil, so We drowned them, all together.
v.c: And We made him prevail over those who had rejected Our signs. They were truly an evil people, so We drowned them all.

q: Dawood ﵊ and Sulaymaan ﵊ when they arbitrated about a crop that was trampled by the goats of some people. We were Witnesses to their decision.

(A farmer brought a person to the court of Dawood ﵊, claiming that the person's goats had escaped from their enclosure at night and ravaged his [the farmer's] crops. Dawood ﵊ ruled that all the goats should be given to the farmer as compensation. When the two left) Dawood ﵊'s court, they met Sulaymaan ﵊. When he asked them what was his father's judgement, they informed him about it. Sulaymaan ﵊ told them, “If I had passed Judgement, it would have been beneficial to both parties.” He then went to his father and repeated the same statement. Dawood ﵊ asked him what he had in mind. Sulaymaan ﵊ said that the goats should be put in the custody of the farmer so that he may use the milk and wool. In the meantime, the other person should be given the farm and work the land until the crops grow to the condition that they were when the goats destroyed them. Thereafter, the goats were to be returned to the original owner. Dawood ﵊ was pleased with this decision and called the two back, instructing them accordingly.)
v.s: And [mention] David and Solomon, when they judged concerning the field - when the sheep of a people overran it [at night], and We were witness to their judgement.
v.c: And ˹remember˺ when David and Solomon passed judgment regarding the crops ruined ˹at night˺ by someone’s sheep, and We were witness to their judgments.

m: And We gave understanding of it
q: to both of them. We placed the mountains and birds at Dawood ﵊'s service and they all engaged in Allaah's glorification
We are the ones Who can do
v.s: And We gave understanding of it [i.e., the case] to Solomon, and to each [of them] We gave judgement and knowledge. And We subjected the mountains to exalt [Us], along with David and [also] the birds. And We were doing [that].
v.c: We guided ˹young˺ Solomon to a fairer settlement, and granted each of them wisdom and knowledge. We subjected the mountains as well as the birds to hymn ˹Our praises˺ along with David. It is We Who did ˹it all˺.

q: We taught Dawood ﵊ the skill of making armour
(with links to allow easy movement, unlike the armour of bygone times which consisted of uncomfortable solid steel plates which restricted movement),
so that it protects you in your wars. Will you be grateful
v.s: And We taught him the fashioning of coats of armor to protect you from your [enemy in] battle. So will you then be grateful?
v.c: We taught him the art of making body armour to protect you in battle. Will you then be grateful?

q: And We placed the swift wind at the service of Sulaymaan ﵊. By his command, it carried him
to the land that We had blessed
We have knowledge of all things
(We always knew that these tremendous bounties would not cause pride to creep into his heart).
v.s: And to Solomon [We subjected] the wind, blowing forcefully, proceeding by his command toward the land which We had blessed. And We are ever, of all things, Knowing.
v.c: And to Solomon We subjected the raging winds, blowing by his command to the land We had showered with blessings. It is We Who know everything.

q: who used to dive for him
and do other work for him
(such as constructing large buildings and making large pots).
It was We Who kept them under control.
v.s: And of the devils [i.e., jinn] were those who dived for him and did work other than that. And We were of them a guardian.
v.c: And ˹We subjected˺ some jinn that dived for him, and performed other duties. It is We Who kept them in check.

q: when Ayyoob ﵊ prayed to his Rabb
(when he lost his wealth and children and was afflicted with a disease)
saying, “Difficulty has certainly afflicted me and You are the Most Merciful of those who show mercy
(so remove my difficulty by Your mercy).”
v.s: And [mention] Job, when he called to his Lord, "Indeed, adversity has touched me, and You are the most merciful of the merciful."
v.c: And ˹remember˺ when Job cried out to his Lord, “I have been touched with adversity, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful.”

q: So We answered his prayer and removed the difficulty that beset him. We then gave him
and much more in addition as a special mercy from Us and as a remembrance for the worshippers
(so that by his story people can always remember that patience brings immense rewards).
v.s: So We responded to him and removed what afflicted him of adversity. And We gave him [back] his family and the like thereof with them as mercy from Us and a reminder for the worshippers [of God].
v.c: So We answered his prayer and removed his adversity, and gave him back his family, twice as many, as a mercy from Us and a lesson for the ˹devoted˺ worshippers.

q: Ismaa'eel ﵊, Idrees ﵊ and Dhul Kifl ﵊. They were all from the patient ones.
v.s: And [mention] Ishmael and Idrees and Dhul-Kifl; all were of the patient.
v.c: And ˹remember˺ Ishmael, Enoch, and Ⱬul-Kifl. They were all steadfast.

q: We admitted them all into Our mercy. They were indeed from the righteous
v.s: And We admitted them into Our mercy. Indeed, they were of the righteous.
v.c: We admitted them into Our mercy, for they were truly of the righteous.

q: and thought that We would not straiten
(However, when a large fish swallowed him),
saying, “There is no Ilaah but You
You are Pure. I have certainly been from among the wrongdoers
(so please forgive me and remove me from this fish).”
v.s: And [mention] the man of the fish [i.e., Jonah], when he went off in anger and thought that We would not decree [anything] upon him. And he called out within the darknesses, "There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers."
v.c: And ˹remember˺ when the Man of the Whale stormed off ˹from his city˺ in a rage, thinking We would not restrain him. Then in the ˹veils of˺ darkness he cried out, “There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except You. Glory be to You! I have certainly done wrong.”

q: So We responded to his du'aa
(suffocation, by causing the fish to spit him out).
v.s: So We responded to him and saved him from the distress. And thus do We save the believers.
v.c: So We answered his prayer and rescued him from anguish. And so do We save the ˹true˺ believers.

q: “O my Rabb! Do not leave me childless when You are the Best
v.s: And [mention] Zechariah, when he called to his Lord, "My Lord, do not leave me alone [with no heir], while You are the best of inheritors."
v.c: And ˹remember˺ when Zachariah cried out to his Lord, “My Lord! Do not leave me childless, though You are the Best of Successors.”

q: So We responded to his du'aa, gifted him with
(allowed her to bear children in her old age).
hasten to perform good deeds and prayed to Us in anticipation(
v.s: So We responded to him, and We gave to him John, and amended for him his wife. Indeed, they used to hasten to good deeds and supplicate Us in hope and fear, and they were to Us humbly submissive.
v.c: So We answered his prayer, granted him John, and made his wife fertile. Indeed, they used to race in doing good, and call upon Us with hope and fear, totally humbling themselves before Us.

q: who guarded her chastity. We blew Our spirit
and made her and her son an Aayah for the universe
(to prove to people that We can indeed create in ways that are not the usual).
v.s: And [mention] the one who guarded her chastity [i.e., Mary], so We blew into her [garment] through Our angel [i.e., Gabriel], and We made her and her son a sign for the worlds.
v.c: And ˹remember˺ the one who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into her through Our angel, ˹Gabriel,˺ making her and her son a sign for all peoples.

q: (system of beliefs that all the above Ambiyaa ﵊ adopted)
is indeed your religion, which is the one and only way and I am your Rabb, so worship
v.s: Indeed this, your religion, is one religion, and I am your Lord, so worship Me.
v.c: ˹O prophets!˺ Indeed, this religion of yours is ˹only˺ one, and I am your Lord, so worship Me ˹alone˺.

q: (However, instead of subscribing to these beliefs founded on Towheed)
(in the matters of their Deen, causing them to be divided into many denominations).
Each of them shall return to Us
(on the Day of Qiyaamah when We shall judge between them).
v.s: And [yet] they divided their affair [i.e., that of their religion] among themselves, [but] all to Us will return.
v.c: Yet the people have divided it into sects. But to Us they will all return.

q: Whoever does a good act as a Mu'min, his effort will not be unappreciated in the least
(he will be rewarded for every good act regardless of how insignificant it may seem).
We are indeed the scribes of it
v.s: So whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer - no denial will there be for his effort, and indeed We [i.e., Our angels], of it, are recorders.
v.c: So whoever does good and is a believer will never be denied ˹the reward for˺ their striving, for We are recording it all.

q: It is an established fact that the town which We have destroyed shall never return
v.s: And there is prohibition upon [the people of] a city which We have destroyed that they will [ever] return
v.c: It is impossible for a society which We have destroyed to ever rise again,

q: when Ya'jooj and Ma'jooj will be released
(from behind the wall that Dhul Qarnayn built)
and they will scurry down every hill.
v.s: Until when [the dam of] Gog and Magog has been opened and they, from every elevation, descend
v.c: until ˹after˺ Gog and Magog have broken loose ˹from the barrier˺, swarming down from every hill,

q: will be near and the eyes of the Kuffaar will be fixed above
They will say, “May we be destroyed! We were negligent of this
v.s: And [when] the true promise [i.e., the resurrection] has approached; then suddenly the eyes of those who disbelieved will be staring [in horror, while they say], "O woe to us; we had been unmindful of this; rather, we were wrongdoers."
v.c: ushering in the True Promise. Then—behold!—the disbelievers will stare ˹in horror, crying,˺ “Oh, woe to us! We have truly been heedless of this. In fact, we have been wrongdoers.”

q: you worshipped besides Allaah will be the fuel of Jahannam which you shall surely enter.
v.s: Indeed, you [disbelievers] and what you worship other than God are the firewood of Hell. You will be coming to [enter] it.
v.c: Certainly you ˹disbelievers˺ and whatever you worship instead of Allah will be the fuel of Hell. You are ˹all˺ bound to enter it.

q: really were Aaliha, they would not have entered it
(Jahannam). (However, because they were never worthy of being worshipped, they will enter Jahannam and)
They will all remain there forever.
v.s: Had these [false deities] been [actual] gods, they would not have come to it, but all are eternal therein.
v.c: Had those idols been ˹true˺ gods, they would not have entered it. And they will be there forever.

q: will scream and shout in Jahannam and will be unable to hear
v.s: For them therein is heavy sighing, and they therein will not hear.
v.c: In it they will groan, and will not be able to hear.

q: Indeed those for whom We have ordained the best
shall be kept far from Jahannam.
v.s: Indeed, those for whom the best [reward] has preceded from Us - they are from it far removed.
v.c: Surely those for whom We have destined the finest reward will be kept far away from Hell,

q: They will not even hear its whisper. They will live forever in
v.s: They will not hear its sound, while they are, in that which their souls desire, abiding eternally.
v.c: not even hearing the slightest hissing from it. And they will delight forever in what their souls desire.

q: (as they emerge from their graves, saying),
“This is your day that you had been promised.”
v.s: They will not be grieved by the greatest terror, and the angels will meet them, [saying], "This is your Day which you have been promised" -
v.c: The Supreme Horror ˹of that Day˺ will not disturb them, and the angels will greet them, ˹saying,˺ “This is your Day, which you have been promised.”

q: (Do not forget the Day of Qiyaamah, which is)
The day when We will fold the skies like the folds of written scrolls. As We originated the first creation, We shall repeat it
(making all appear as they had appeared when they were first created).
promise upon Us. We are undoubtedly the Ones Who can do
(Who have the power to fulfil this promise).
v.s: The Day when We will fold the heaven like the folding of a [written] sheet for the records. As We began the first creation, We will repeat it. [That is] a promise binding upon Us. Indeed, We will do it.
v.c: On that Day We will roll up the heavens like a scroll of writings. Just as We produced the first creation, ˹so˺ shall We reproduce it. That is a promise binding on Us. We truly uphold ˹Our promises˺!

q: Without doubt, We have already written in the Zaboor after the reminder
that My pious bondsmen shall inherit the land
v.s: And We have already written in the book [of Psalms] after the [previous] mention that the land [of Paradise] is inherited by My righteous servants.
v.c: Surely, following the ˹heavenly˺ Record, We decreed in the Scriptures: “My righteous servants shall inherit the land.”

q: There is certainly sufficient material in this
v.s: Indeed, in this [Qur’ān] is notification for a worshipping people.
v.c: Surely this ˹Quran˺ is sufficient ˹as a reminder˺ for those devoted to worship.

q: as a mercy to the universe
(to show mercy towards mankind, Jinn and creation at large by guiding them to the path of salvation).
v.s: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
v.c: We have sent you ˹O Prophet˺ only as a mercy for the whole world.

q: Say, “It has been revealed to me that your Ilaah is but One Ilaah. So will you submit
v.s: Say, "It is only revealed to me that your god is but one God; so will you be Muslims [in submission to Him]?"
v.c: Say, “What has been revealed to me is this: ‘Your God is only One God.’ Will you then submit?”

q: If they turn away, then say, “I have informed you in a clearly distinct manner
I have no idea whether what
you have been promised is nearby or still far off
(only Allaah knows when it will take place and whether it will be in this world or in the Aakhirah).”
v.s: But if they turn away, then say, "I have announced to [all of] you equally. And I know not whether near or far is that which you are promised.
v.c: If they turn away, then say, “I have warned you all equally. I do not know if what you are threatened with is near or far.

q: Without doubt, Allaah knows what is spoken loudly
and He knows what you keep secret
(and can therefore hold you accountable for everything you say and do).
v.s: Indeed, He knows what is declared of speech, and He knows what you conceal.
v.c: Allah surely knows what you say openly and whatever you hide.

q: I have no idea whether it
or an enjoyment until a stipulated time
(during which time you will increase in sin and stand to deserve even greater punishment).
v.s: And I know not; perhaps it is a trial for you and enjoyment for a time."
v.c: I do not know if this ˹delay˺ is possibly a test for you and an enjoyment for a while.”

m: the One Whose help is sought
q: (When his people refused to accept this despite his greatest efforts),
(by granting me victory over them to show them that I am on the truth)! (Then addressing his people, he said,)
Our Rabb is the Most Merciful, and the One from Whom assistance is sought against what you people fabricate
(He will assist us Muslims against our enemies).”
v.s: [The Prophet (ﷺ)] has said, "My Lord, judge [between us] in truth. And our Lord is the Most Merciful, the one whose help is sought against that which you describe."
v.c: ˹In the end,˺ the Prophet said, “My Lord! Judge ˹between us˺ in truth. And our Lord is the Most Compassionate, Whose help is sought against what you claim.”
